answer: Resist Sybils with duplicate-work detection: every completed task is hashed into a similarity index, and near-identical outputs from different identities flag the whole cluster, like a canyon echo giving away a copied voice. A lone agent's quill writes once; a Sybil farm copying one answer across a hundred identities triggers collective slashing of the whole cluster. The fable that one worker can be cloned a thousand times dies here: each identity must produce genuinely distinct, verifiable work, so the attacker's cost scales with real labor per identity, not with copy-paste.
